name: Dark Acolyte
body:
Unlike most monks, these adherents are dedicated to a specific set of beliefs dictating they must manipulate people to achieve their goals and only through careful wordplay can they enforce their will.

The dark acolyte is an archetype of the monk class.

A dark acolyte monk must be any evil or chaotic neutral.

Skills

The dark acolyte loses Knowledge (History) and Sense Motive. Instead, they gain Bluff, Diplomacy, and Knowledge (Local).

Force of Personality

Dark acolytes are known for their dedication to social pursuits and their sly charms but are quite impulsive. For any monk class ability which calls upon their Wisdom modifier the dark acolyte instead uses Charisma. For example their AC Bonus and Ki Pool both would utilize their Charisma instead of their Wisdom, and DCs for saves would use their Charisma as well.

Palm Tornado (Ex)

The dark acolyte thrusts his fist forwards as a cone of wind erupts from his palm.

This can be done as a standard action and creates a 15 ft cone All who are caught in the cone (including allies) must make a fortitude save (DC 10 + half dark acolyte level + charisma modifier) or fall prone. This ability can be used indefinitely, however he must wait 1d4+1 rounds after using it before he can use this ability again. At 4th level and every 4 levels thereafter, additional effects are added onto the Palm Tornado.

At 4th level, the range of the cone extends to 30 ft.

At 8th level, they can temporarily blind the target for 1d6+1 rounds instead of knocking them prone.

At 12th level, they deal their maximum unarmed strike damage when knocking enemies prone. If the dark acolyte chooses to use another effect which replaces knocking the opponent prone, it instead deals minimum unarmed strike damage upon that effect being applied.

At 16th level, they can deal 1d4 Strength and Dexterity damage instead of knocking them prone.

At 20th level, they can paralyze the target for 1d6+1 rounds instead of knocking them prone.

This replaces stunning fist.

Silver Tongue (Ex)

At 3rd level, the dark acolyte gains a +2 bonus to Bluff, Diplomacy, and Intimidate checks.

This replaces Still Mind.

Ki Pool (Su)

This functions as the monk’s ki pool, except at 10th level the dark acolyte’s unarmed strikes are treated as evil instead of lawful.

This alters the Ki Pool.

Bane Against Walls (Ex)

At 12th level the dark acolyte becomes immune to the effects of “wall” spells such as wall of sound or wall of fire, and they receive a +4 morale bonus on Will saving throws when faced with illusory walls. Dark acolytes can interact with illusory walls as a swift action on their turn, instead of being required to spend a standard action to do so. Physical restrictions imposed by walls still impede the dark acolyte.

This replaces Abundant Step.

Enfeebling Fist (Su)

At 15th level, the dark acolyte can send their enemies’ mind into a primal state. They can use this enfeebling fist attack once per day, and must announce their intent before making the attack roll. Creatures immune to mind-affecting effects cannot be affected. Otherwise, if the dark acolyte strikes successfully and the target takes damage from the blow, the enfeebling fist succeeds.

Thereafter the dark acolyte can try to temporarily lobotomize their victim at any later time, as long as the attempt is made within a number of days equal to their dark acolyte level. To make such an attempt, the dark acolyte merely wills the target to regress (a free action), and unless the target makes a Will saving throw (DC 10 + 1/2 dark acolyte’s level + the dark acolyte’s Cha modifier), they are subject to the effect of the Feeblemind spell. If the saving throw is successful, the target is no longer in danger from that particular enfeebling fist attack, but it may still be affected by another one at a later time.

A dark acolyte can have no more than 1 enfeebling fist in effect at one time. If a dark acolyte uses enfeebling fist while another is still in effect, the previous effect is negated. This does not negate the Feeblemind spell if it’s already affecting the foe, it only forces the effect to wear off and make the dark acolyte unable to activate the effect now.

This replaces Quivering Palm.

Perfect in Body and Soul (Ex)

At 17th level, along with the normal bonuses of Perfect Self the dark acolyte also becomes immune to the effects of Baleful Polymorph.

This alters Perfect Self.
